newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian turmoil costs $70 million in damages.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian turmoil costs $70 million in damages.

text.p: Recent fighting and looting in the Cambodian capital caused damage worth more than $70 million, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

"The total is not clear yet, but yesterday the committee estimated that there was more than $50 million in losses, not including a garment factory which has asked the government to pay $26 million for compensation," said Secretary of State for Interior Kieng Vang.
Kieng Vang is co-chairman of a government committee charged with tallying losses from the recent violence.

Forces loyal to Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh fought in the capital on July 5-6. Hun Sen announced Ranariddh's ouster on July 6 and his victorious soldiers went on a looting rampage on the following day.
The battles and looting caused serious damage to businesses and homes in parts of the city. About 60 people were killed and up to 200 wounded, most of them civilians caught in cross-fire.

Minister of Industry Pou Sothirak said the government intended to compensate those who lost property after the total costs were tallied, but added that he did not know how the government would cover the costs.
"The royal government will discuss this in a cabinet meeting, but first we're waiting for the final report of the total damages," he said.
Hun Sen has offered to exempt some companies from import and export duties or provide tax breaks as compensation to those who incurred losses during the fighting and looting.
